blocks.faith.heading: Faith at the center, never forced
blocks.faith.body: If you want faith to be part of your counseling, your counselor will bring it in. If not, you'll get the same clinical care. You lead.

sections.heading: What is dialectical behavior therapy (DBT)?
sections.body: Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) teaches practical skills for handling intense emotions, getting through crises without making things worse, and keeping relationships steady. "Dialectical" means holding two things at once: accepting yourself as you are, and working to change. DBT was developed by psychologist Marsha Linehan.

DBT was developed to help people who feel emotions intensely. It teaches four sets of skills: mindfulness (staying present), distress tolerance (getting through a crisis without making it worse), emotion regulation (understanding and calming strong feelings), and interpersonal effectiveness (asking for what you need while keeping relationships intact).
sections.heading: Skills for big emotions

sections.body:
Our counselors are DBT-informed: they teach and practice DBT skills within individual counseling, alongside other approaches. Freedom doesn't offer comprehensive DBT, which includes a weekly skills group, phone coaching between sessions, and a DBT consultation team, and neither counselor is DBT-certified.

DBT-informed counseling can be a good fit if you want skills for handling emotions and relationships.
sections.heading: DBT-informed counseling, not a full DBT program

sections.body: If you're dealing with frequent self-harm, repeated suicidal crises, or your provider has recommended comprehensive DBT, a full program is the better fit. Call us anyway, and we'll help you find one.

blocks.expect.heading: Your first session
blocks.expect.body: Your first session is about understanding what's been happening and what you'd like to handle differently. If you're in crisis or need a higher level of care, your counselor will help you find it. Sessions are in our Middletown office or online.
blocks.cost.body: We don't bill insurance, but you can pay with an HSA or FSA card, and we'll give you a superbill to submit for possible out-of-network reimbursement.
